cor-annihilator-of-annihilator.title: The Annihilator of the Annihilator
cor-annihilator-of-annihilator.html: Let V be a finite-dimensional vector space over F, and let U be a subspace of V. Write U00:=(U0)0⊆V∗∗. Then U00=evV(U)={evu:u∈U}. So, under the identification v↔evv, we have U00=U. Equivalently, U={v∈V:φ(v)=0 for every φ∈U0}.

cor-dimension-dual-space.title: Dimension of the Dual Space
cor-dimension-dual-space.html: Let V be a finite-dimensional vector space over F. Then V∗ is finite-dimensional and dim⁡V∗=dim⁡V. In particular V∗≅V.

cor-every-basis-of-dual-is-dual.title: Every Basis of the Dual Is a Dual Basis
cor-every-basis-of-dual-is-dual.title_html: Every Basis of the Dual Is a Dual Basis
cor-every-basis-of-dual-is-dual.html: Let V be a finite-dimensional vector space over F, and let (ψ1,…,ψn) be a basis of V∗. Then there is exactly one basis (v1,…,vn) of V whose dual basis is (ψ1,…,ψn), that is, with ψi(vj)=δijfor all i,j.

cor-injective-iff-dual-surjective.title: Injective and Surjective Swap Under Duality
cor-injective-iff-dual-surjective.title_html: Injective and Surjective Swap Under Duality
cor-injective-iff-dual-surjective.html:
Let V and W be finite-dimensional vector spaces over F, and T∈L(V,W). Then:

  1. T is surjective if and only if T′ is injective;
  2. T is injective if and only if T′ is surjective.

cor-rank-dual-map.title: Rank of the Dual Map
cor-rank-dual-map.html:
1. Let V and W be finite-dimensional vector spaces over F, and T∈L(V,W). Then rankT′=rankT.
  2. For every A∈Mm×n(F), rankAT=rankA. Equivalently, dim⁡row(A)=dim⁡col(A): row rank equals column rank.

cor-same-null-space-iff-same-row-space.title: Same solutions, same row space
cor-same-null-space-iff-same-row-space.html: Let A∈Mm×n(F) and B∈Mp×n(F). Then nul(A)=nul(B) if and only if row(A)=row(B).

cor-subspaces-determined-by-annihilator.title: Subspaces Are Determined by Their Annihilators
cor-subspaces-determined-by-annihilator.title_html: Subspaces Are Determined by Their Annihilators
cor-subspaces-determined-by-annihilator.html: Let V be a finite-dimensional vector space, and let U and W be subspaces of V. Then U=W if and only if U0=W0.

def-annihilator.title: Annihilator
def-annihilator.html: Let V be a vector space over F, and let S⊆V be any subset. The annihilator of S is S0:={φ∈V∗:φ(s)=0 for all s∈S}.

def-codimension.title: Codimension
def-codimension.html: Let U be a subspace of a vector space V over F. If V/U is finite-dimensional, the codimension of U in V is codimU:=dim⁡(V/U). If V/U is infinite-dimensional, we say that U has infinite codimension.

def-dual-basis.title: Dual Basis
def-dual-basis.html: Let B=(v1,…,vn) be a basis of a finite-dimensional vector space V over F. The basis (φ1,…,φn) of V∗ given by @thm-dual-basis, characterized by φi(vj)=δij, is the dual basis of B. We write it B∗.

def-dual-map.title: Dual Map
def-dual-map.html: Let V and W be vector spaces over F, and let T∈L(V,W). The dual map of T is the map T′:W∗→V∗,T′(ψ):=ψT=ψ∘T. That is, (T′ψ)(v)=ψ(Tv) for every ψ∈W∗ and every v∈V.

def-dual-space.title: Dual Space
def-dual-space.html: Let V be a vector space over F. The dual space of V is the set of all linear functionals on V, V∗:=L(V,F), with the pointwise operations (φ+ψ)(v):=φ(v)+ψ(v) and (cφ)(v):=cφ(v) for φ,ψ∈V∗, c∈F and v∈V.

def-evaluation-map.title: Double Dual and Evaluation Map
def-evaluation-map.html:
Let V be a vector space over F. The double dual of V is V∗∗:=(V∗)∗, the space of linear functionals on V∗.

For v∈V, evaluation at v is the function evv:V∗→F,evv(φ):=φ(v). The evaluation map of V is evV:V→V∗∗,v↦evv. When only one space is in play we write ev for evV.

def-hyperplane.title: Hyperplane
def-hyperplane.html: A hyperplane in V is a subspace H of V of codimension exactly 1, that is, with dim⁡(V/H)=1.

def-linear-functional.title: Linear Functional
def-linear-functional.html: Let V be a vector space over F, and regard F as a vector space over itself. A linear functional on V is a linear map φ:V→F. That is, for all u,v∈V and all c∈F, φ(u+v)=φ(u)+φ(v),φ(cv)=cφ(v).

exm-annihilator-of-evaluation-kernel.title: The Equations of a Root Condition
exm-annihilator-of-evaluation-kernel.title_html: The Equations of a Root Condition
exm-annihilator-of-evaluation-kernel.html: Let U={p∈R[x]≤2:p(1)=0}. Find U0.

exm-annihilator-via-null-space.title: An Annihilator as a Null Space
exm-annihilator-via-null-space.title_html: An Annihilator as a Null Space
exm-annihilator-via-null-space.html: Find a basis of U0 for U=span((1,2,0),(0,1,1))⊆R3, and check the dimension formula.

exm-annihilators.title: First Annihilators
exm-annihilators.html:
1. For any vector space V, find {0}0, ∅0 and V0.
  2. In M2(F), find the annihilator of the single matrix E11.
  3. In R[x]≤2, find the annihilator of S={1,x}.

exm-basis-from-dual-basis.title: A Basis With Prescribed Dual Basis
exm-basis-from-dual-basis.title_html: A Basis With Prescribed Dual Basis
exm-basis-from-dual-basis.html: On V=R[x]≤2, consider the functionals ψ1(p)=p(0),ψ2(p)=p(1),ψ3(p)=p′(1). Show that (ψ1,ψ2,ψ3) is a basis of V∗, and find the basis (p1,p2,p3) of V whose dual basis it is.

exm-dual-basis-inverse-rows.title: The Dual Basis Is Read Off the Inverse Matrix
exm-dual-basis-inverse-rows.title_html: The Dual Basis Is Read Off the Inverse Matrix
exm-dual-basis-inverse-rows.html:
1. Find the dual basis of B=((1,1),(1,−1)) in R2.
  2. More generally, let B=(v1,…,vn) be a basis of Fn, and let P=(v1⋯vn). Show that P is invertible and that the dual basis of B is φi(x)=rix, where ri is the i-th row of P−1.

exm-dual-basis-polynomials.title: Dual Bases in \nR[x]_{\le 2}
exm-dual-basis-polynomials.title_html: Dual Bases in R[x]≤2
exm-dual-basis-polynomials.html:
1. Show that the dual basis of (1,x,x2) in R[x]≤2 is (φ0,φ1,φ2) with φ0(p)=p(0), φ1(p)=p′(0) and φ2(p)=12p″(0). (We index from 0 to match the exponents.)
  2. Let ℓ−1=12x(x−1), ℓ0=1−x2 and ℓ1=12x(x+1). Show that (ℓ−1,ℓ0,ℓ1) is a basis of R[x]≤2 whose dual basis is (ε−1,ε0,ε1), the evaluations at −1,0,1. Deduce that p=p(−1)ℓ−1+p(0)ℓ0+p(1)ℓ1 for every p∈R[x]≤2.

exm-dual-map-examples.title: Dual Maps in Four Settings
exm-dual-map-examples.html:
1. For A∈Mm×n(F), describe TA′ in terms of the vectors b and ATb that represent functionals.
  2. Let D:R[x]≤3→R[x]≤2, D(p)=p′, and let ε2∈(R[x]≤2)∗ be ε2(q)=q(2). Compute D′(ε2).
  3. Let S:F[x]→F[x], S(p)=xp, and let φk∈F[x]∗ send a polynomial to its coefficient of xk. Compute S′(φk) for every k∈N.
  4. Find (idV)′, the dual map of the zero map V→W, and the dual map of the inclusion ι:U→V, ι(u)=u, of a subspace U⊆V.

exm-dual-of-line-quotient.title: Both isomorphisms for a line
exm-dual-of-line-quotient.html:
Let u=(1,2,−1) and U=span(u)⊆R3.

  1. Find a basis of U0.
  2. Find a basis of R3/U, its dual basis (ψ1,ψ2) of (R3/U)∗, and the images π′(ψ1),π′(ψ2).
  3. Describe the restriction map ρ:(R3)∗→U∗ and the isomorphism (R3)∗/U0→U∗.

exm-evaluation-map.title: Evaluation in Three Spaces
exm-evaluation-map.html:
1. Let V=Fn. Describe evx for x∈Fn in terms of row vectors.
  2. Let V=R[x]≤2, and let (φ0,φ1,φ2) be the dual basis of (1,x,x2), so that φk(p) is the coefficient of xk in p (@exm-dual-basis-polynomials). Compute evx2 on φ0,φ1,φ2 and on the functional ε3(p)=p(3). Which element of V∗∗ is evx2?
  3. Describe ev0, and the evaluation map of V={0}.

exm-evaluation-not-surjective.title: A Functional on F\lbrack x\rbrack^{*} That Is Not an Evaluation
exm-evaluation-not-surjective.title_html: A Functional on F[x]∗ That Is Not an Evaluation
exm-evaluation-not-surjective.html: Let φk∈F[x]∗ (k∈N) be the coordinate functionals, φk(p)= the coefficient of xk in p, and let ε1(p)=p(1), as in @prp-coordinate-functionals-do-not-span. Show that there is θ∈F[x]∗∗ with θ≠evp for every p∈F[x].

exm-implicit-equations.title: Equations for a plane in \nR^4
exm-implicit-equations.title_html: Equations for a plane in R4
exm-implicit-equations.html: Let U=span(u1,u2)⊆R4, where u1=(1,1,0,1) and u2=(0,1,1,1). Find a system of linear equations whose solution set is U.

exm-intersection-via-equations.title: An intersection computed from equations
exm-intersection-via-equations.html: In R4, let U=span((1,0,1,2),(0,1,1,1)) and W=span((1,1,0,1),(1,3,0,1)), as in @exm-intersection-by-elimination. Find U∩W by first finding equations for U and for W.

exm-kernel-image-dual-map.title: Kernel and Image of a Dual Map
exm-kernel-image-dual-map.title_html: Kernel and Image of a Dual Map
exm-kernel-image-dual-map.html: Let T=TA:R3→R3 with A=(10201−1111). Find bases of kerT′ and imT′, written as explicit functionals, and check @thm-kernel-image-dual-map.

exm-linear-functionals.title: Four Families of Functionals
exm-linear-functionals.html:
Show that each map is a linear functional.

  1. εc:F[x]→F, p↦p(c), for a fixed c∈F (evaluation at c).
  2. ι:R[x]≤2→R, p↦∫01p(t)dt.
  3. tr:Mn(F)→F.
  4. The zero functional on any V. Also find the dual space of the zero space {0}.

exm-matrix-of-dual-map.title: A 2 \times 3 Example
exm-matrix-of-dual-map.title_html: A 2×3 Example
exm-matrix-of-dual-map.html:
Let T:R[x]≤2→R2, T(p)=(p(1),p′(1)). Use the basis B=(1,x,x2), whose dual basis B∗=(φ0,φ1,φ2) consists of φ0(p)=p(0), φ1(p)=p′(0), φ2(p)=p″(0)/2 (@exm-dual-basis-polynomials), and the standard basis C=(e1,e2) of R2, with dual basis C∗=(η1,η2), η1(u,v)=u, η2(u,v)=v.

  1. Find A=[T]BC.
  2. Compute T′η1 and T′η2 directly as combinations of φ0,φ1,φ2, write down [T′]C∗B∗, and compare with AT.
  3. Use the matrix to compute T′ψ for ψ=−2η1+η2, and check the answer directly.

exm-trace-test-zero-matrix.title: A Matrix Killed by Every Trace
exm-trace-test-zero-matrix.title_html: A Matrix Killed by Every Trace
exm-trace-test-zero-matrix.html: Let A∈Mn(F) satisfy tr(AX)=0 for every X∈Mn(F). Show that A=0. Deduce that every linear functional on Mn(F) is X↦tr(AX) for exactly one A∈Mn(F).

exr-annihilators-a1.title: A1
exr-annihilators-a1.html:
1. Define the annihilator S0 of a subset S of a vector space V.
  2. True or false: U0 is a subspace of V. Justify your answer.
  3. Let U be a 2-dimensional subspace of R5. What is dim⁡U0?
  4. For a finite-dimensional V, what are {0}0 and V0?
  5. True or false: if U⊊W are subspaces of a finite-dimensional V, then W0⊊U0. Justify your answer.
  6. To compute U0 for U=span(u1,…,um)⊆Fn, which matrix do you row reduce, and why?

exr-annihilators-b1.title: B1: Computing annihilators
exr-annihilators-b1.html:
1. Let U=span((1,2,1,0),(2,4,3,1),(1,2,2,1))⊆R4. Find a basis of U0, and verify that dim⁡U+dim⁡U0=4.
  2. Let U={p∈R[x]≤3:p(1)=p(−1)=0}. Show that U0=span(ε1,ε−1), where εc(p)=p(c).

exr-annihilators-b2.title: B2: Equations of the symmetric matrices
exr-annihilators-b2.title_html: B2: Equations of the symmetric matrices
exr-annihilators-b2.html: Let U={A∈M2(R):AT=A}. Find U0, and verify the dimension formula.

exr-annihilators-b3.title: B3: The equations of a hyperplane
exr-annihilators-b3.title_html: B3: The equations of a hyperplane
exr-annihilators-b3.html: Let V be a finite-dimensional vector space over F, and let φ∈V∗ be non-zero. Prove that (kerφ)0=span(φ).

exr-annihilators-c1.title: C1: The intersection formula without counting
exr-annihilators-c1.title_html: C1: The intersection formula without counting
exr-annihilators-c1.html:
Let U,W be subspaces of a vector space V over F, and let φ∈(U∩W)0.

  1. Suppose V is finite-dimensional. Construct ψ∈U0 and χ∈W0 with φ=ψ+χ, without using any dimension formula.
  2. Explain how to modify the construction when V is infinite-dimensional. Deduce that (U∩W)0=U0+W0 holds in every vector space.

Hint: extend a basis of U∩W to a basis of U and, separately, to a basis of W.

exr-annihilators-c2.title: C2: Equations of a double root
exr-annihilators-c2.title_html: C2: Equations of a double root
exr-annihilators-c2.html: Let U={p∈R[x]≤3:p(1)=0 and p′(1)=0}, and let ε1(p)=p(1) and η1(p)=p′(1). Prove that U0=span(ε1,η1). Deduce that ψ(p)=p(0)−p(2)+2p′(1) does not vanish on U.

exr-annihilators-c3.title: C3: Dual of a direct sum decomposition
exr-annihilators-c3.title_html: C3: Dual of a direct sum decomposition
exr-annihilators-c3.html:
1. Let V be finite-dimensional with V=U⊕W. Prove that V∗=U0⊕W0.
  2. In R2, let U=span((1,0)) and W=span((1,1)). Write ψ(x,y)=x as ψU+ψW with ψU∈U0 and ψW∈W0.

exr-double-dual-a1.title: A1
exr-double-dual-a1.html:
1. Define evv for v∈V, and the evaluation map evV. In which space does evv live?
  2. State a hypothesis on V under which evV is an isomorphism, and a space for which it is not.
  3. True or false: if V is finite-dimensional and v≠0, then evv(φ)≠0 for every non-zero φ∈V∗. Justify your answer.
  4. True or false: if U and W are subspaces of R5 with U0=W0, then U=W. Justify your answer.
  5. Name the method used to prove U00=evV(U) in @cor-annihilator-of-annihilator.

exr-double-dual-b1.title: B1: A basis with a given dual basis
exr-double-dual-b1.title_html: B1: A basis with a given dual basis
exr-double-dual-b1.html:
1. Let ψ1(x,y)=2x+y and ψ2(x,y)=x+y on R2. Find the basis (v1,v2) of R2 whose dual basis is (ψ1,ψ2).
  2. Let ψ1(p)=p(0) and ψ2(p)=∫01p(x)dx on R[x]≤1. Find the basis (p1,p2) of R[x]≤1 whose dual basis is (ψ1,ψ2).

exr-double-dual-b2.title: B2: U^{00} = U for a line
exr-double-dual-b2.title_html: B2: U00=U for a line
exr-double-dual-b2.html:
Let U=span((1,2,−1))⊆R3.

  1. Find a basis of U0.
  2. Find all v∈R3 with φ(v)=0 for every φ∈U0, and check that the answer is U.
  3. Hence verify that U00=ev(U), and confirm the dimension count.

exr-double-dual-b3.title: B3: Recognizing an evaluation
exr-double-dual-b3.html: Let V=R[x]≤2, with the coefficient functionals φ0,φ1,φ2 of @exm-evaluation-map. Let θ∈V∗∗ be the linear functional with θ(φ0)=1, θ(φ1)=−3, θ(φ2)=2. Find p∈V with θ=evp. Hence compute θ(ε1) and θ(ψ), where ε1(q)=q(1) and ψ(q)=q′(0).

exr-double-dual-c1.title: C1: Subspaces of V and of V^{*}
exr-double-dual-c1.title_html: C1: Subspaces of V and of V∗
exr-double-dual-c1.html:
Let V be a finite-dimensional vector space over F. Prove that U↦U0 is a bijection from the set of subspaces of V to the set of subspaces of V∗, and that it reverses inclusions in both directions: U⊆W if and only if W0⊆U0.

Hint: for surjectivity, given a subspace X⊆V∗, consider U={v∈V:φ(v)=0 for all φ∈X}.

exr-double-dual-c2.title: C2: Spans cut out by equations
exr-double-dual-c2.title_html: C2: Spans cut out by equations
exr-double-dual-c2.html:
Let V be finite-dimensional and S⊆V any subset.

  1. Prove that {v∈V:φ(v)=0 for every φ∈S0}=span(S).
  2. Deduce: a vector v lies in span(S) if and only if every functional that vanishes on S vanishes at v.
  3. Show by an example that (a) can fail if “span(S)” is replaced by “S”.

exr-double-dual-c3.title: C3: Where finite dimension is needed
exr-double-dual-c3.title_html: C3: Where finite dimension is needed
exr-double-dual-c3.html:
Let V=F[x], let φk and ε1 be as in @exm-evaluation-not-surjective, and let X=span{φk:k∈N}⊆V∗.

  1. Show that {p∈F[x]:φ(p)=0 for all φ∈X}={0}.
  2. Deduce that X≠U0 for every subspace U of F[x]. So the map U↦U0 of @exr-double-dual-c1 is not surjective for F[x].
  3. Which step of the solution of @exr-double-dual-c1 fails here?

exr-dual-map-a1.title: A1
exr-dual-map-a1.html:
1. Define the dual map T′ of T∈L(V,W), including its domain and codomain.
  2. State the relation between [T′]C∗B∗ and [T]BC, with its hypotheses.
  3. True or false: (ST)′=S′T′ whenever ST is defined. Justify your answer.
  4. True or false: kerT′=(kerT)0 for every linear map between finite-dimensional spaces. Justify your answer.
  5. True or false: for T∈L(R4,R3), the dual map T′ is never surjective. Justify your answer.
  6. Name the two tools combined to prove rankT′=rankT.

exr-dual-map-b1.title: B1: Differentiation in dual bases
exr-dual-map-b1.html: Let D:R[x]≤2→R[x]≤2, D(p)=p′, and let B=(1,x,x2) with dual basis B∗=(φ0,φ1,φ2), φk(p)= the coefficient of xk in p. Compute D′φ0, D′φ1, D′φ2 directly, write down [D′]B∗, and check that it is ([D]B)T. Hence describe kerD′ and imD′, and verify @thm-kernel-image-dual-map.

exr-dual-map-b2.title: B2: Kernel and image of a dual map
exr-dual-map-b2.title_html: B2: Kernel and image of a dual map
exr-dual-map-b2.html: Let A=(12−1−2−42) and T=TA:R3→R2. Find bases of kerT′ and imT′ as explicit functionals, and verify dim⁡kerT′+dim⁡imT′=2 and rankT′=rankT.

exr-dual-map-b3.title: B3: The transpose of a product, again
exr-dual-map-b3.title_html: B3: The transpose of a product, again
exr-dual-map-b3.html: Let A∈Mm×n(F) and B∈Mn×p(F). Using TATB=TAB (Chapter 3, §6), @thm-dual-map-properties (b) and @thm-matrix-of-dual-map, give a new proof that (AB)T=BTAT.

exr-dual-map-c1.title: C1: The Fredholm alternative
exr-dual-map-c1.html:
1. Let V,W be finite-dimensional, T∈L(V,W) and w∈W. Prove that Tv=w has a solution v∈V if and only if ψ(w)=0 for every ψ∈kerT′.
  2. Deduce: for A∈Mm×n(F) and b∈Fm, the system Ax=b is consistent if and only if yTb=0 for every y∈Fm with ATy=0.
  3. Let A=(111213). Find a single linear condition on b=(b1,b2,b3)∈R3 that is equivalent to consistency of Ax=b.

Hint: for (a), combine @thm-kernel-image-dual-map with the description of a subspace by its annihilator in the previous section.

exr-dual-map-c2.title: C2: Invariant subspaces and annihilators
exr-dual-map-c2.html: Let V be finite-dimensional, T∈L(V), and U a subspace of V. Recall that U is T-invariant if Tu∈U for every u∈U. Prove that U is T-invariant if and only if U0 is T′-invariant.

exr-dual-map-c3.title: C3: Duality without finite dimension
exr-dual-map-c3.html:
Let V and W be arbitrary vector spaces over F, and T∈L(V,W).

  1. Prove that if T is surjective, then T′ is injective.
  2. Prove that if T is injective, then T′ is surjective.
  3. Check (b) on S:F[x]→F[x], S(p)=xp, from @exm-dual-map-examples (c): given φ∈F[x]∗, find ψ with S′ψ=φ. Is S′ injective?

Hint: for (b), use @thm-basis-extension-general in W.

exr-duality-subspaces-quotients-a1.title: A1
exr-duality-subspaces-quotients-a1.html:
1. State the theorem identifying (V/U)∗ with a subspace of V∗, including the map.
  2. Define the codimension of a subspace, and define a hyperplane.
  3. True or false: U∗ is a subspace of V∗. Justify your answer.
  4. Let U be a subspace of dimension 2 in F5. Find dim⁡(F5/U)∗ and codimU.
  5. Is {(x1,x2,x3,x4)∈R4:x1=x2=0} a hyperplane in R4? Justify your answer.
  6. True or false: every non-zero linear functional φ:V→F is surjective. Justify your answer.

exr-duality-subspaces-quotients-b1.title: B1: The dual of a quotient of \nR^4
exr-duality-subspaces-quotients-b1.title_html: B1: The dual of a quotient of R4
exr-duality-subspaces-quotients-b1.html:
Let U=span((1,−1,0,2),(0,1,1,−1))⊆R4, and write functionals on R4 as a1x1+a2x2+a3x3+a4x4.

  1. Find a basis (φ1,φ2) of U0.
  2. Let ψ1,ψ2∈(R4/U)∗ be the functionals with π′(ψi)=φi. Compute ψ1 and ψ2 at the coset (2,0,1,3)+U.
  3. Find a basis of R4/U whose dual basis is (ψ1,ψ2).

exr-duality-subspaces-quotients-b2.title: B2: Functionals with the same kernel
exr-duality-subspaces-quotients-b2.title_html: B2: Functionals with the same kernel
exr-duality-subspaces-quotients-b2.html:
Let V be a vector space over F, of any dimension, and let φ,ψ∈V∗ be non-zero. Prove that kerφ=kerψ if and only if ψ=cφ for some non-zero c∈F. (@exr-linear-functionals-c1 proved (⇒) by a different route; here use the hyperplane decomposition.)

Hint: the remark after @thm-hyperplane-kernel-functional.

exr-duality-subspaces-quotients-b3.title: B3: Dimension computations
exr-duality-subspaces-quotients-b3.html:
1. Let dim⁡V=7 and dim⁡U=3. Find dim⁡U∗, dim⁡(V∗/U0), dim⁡(V/U)∗ and codimU.
  2. In V=F[x]≤3, let U={p:p(0)=p(1)=0}. Using the map T:V→F2, T(p)=(p(0),p(1)), find codimU and dim⁡U, and write U as an intersection of two hyperplanes.
  3. Hence find a basis of U0 consisting of evaluation functionals.

exr-duality-subspaces-quotients-c1.title: C1: Subspaces of finite codimension are intersections of hyperplanes
exr-duality-subspaces-quotients-c1.title_html: C1: Subspaces of finite codimension are intersections of hyperplanes
exr-duality-subspaces-quotients-c1.html:
Let V be a vector space over F, of any dimension, and let U be a subspace of finite codimension k≥1.

  1. Prove that there are non-zero φ1,…,φk∈U0 with U=kerφ1∩⋯∩kerφk. Deduce that U is an intersection of k hyperplanes.
  2. Prove that U is not an intersection of fewer than k hyperplanes.

Hint: for (a), take a dual basis of (V/U)∗; for (b), consider the map V→Fm, v↦(φ1(v),…,φm(v)).

exr-duality-subspaces-quotients-c2.title: C2: Complements and a choice of copy of U^{*}
exr-duality-subspaces-quotients-c2.title_html: C2: Complements and a choice of copy of U∗
exr-duality-subspaces-quotients-c2.html:
Let V be finite-dimensional, and let U,W be subspaces with V=U⊕W.

  1. Prove that V∗=U0⊕W0 without using @thm-annihilator-properties (d). (This is @exr-annihilators-c3 (a), which used it.)
  2. Deduce that the restriction map ρ:V∗→U∗ restricts to an isomorphism W0→U∗.
  3. In R2, let U=span(e1), W1=span(e2) and W2=span((1,1)). Find W10 and W20, and find the element of each that restricts to the functional ξ∈U∗ with ξ(e1)=1. Conclude that the copy of U∗ inside V∗ depends on the complement.

exr-hyperplanes-and-systems-a1.title: A1
exr-hyperplanes-and-systems-a1.html:
1. Explain how a row vector aT (with a∈Fn) defines a linear functional on Fn, and why every functional arises this way.
  2. What is the least number of homogeneous linear equations whose solution set is a given 3-dimensional subspace of F7?
  3. True or false: every system of three homogeneous equations in R5 has a solution set of dimension 2. Justify your answer.
  4. State the relation between row(A) and nul(A) in terms of annihilators.
  5. True or false: if A and B have n columns and nul(A)=nul(B), then A and B have the same number of rows. Justify your answer.
  6. Name the dual counterparts of: a sum of subspaces; an injective linear map; the matrix of a linear map.

exr-hyperplanes-and-systems-b1.title: B1: Equations for a span
exr-hyperplanes-and-systems-b1.html:
Let U=span((1,2,0,−1),(2,1,1,0),(3,3,1,−1))⊆R4.

  1. Find dim⁡U.
  2. Find a system of homogeneous linear equations with solution set U, using as few equations as possible.
  3. Hence write the affine plane (1,0,0,0)+U as the solution set of a linear system.

exr-hyperplanes-and-systems-b2.title: B2: A spanning list for a system
exr-hyperplanes-and-systems-b2.title_html: B2: A spanning list for a system
exr-hyperplanes-and-systems-b2.html:
Let U={x∈R4:x1+x2−x3+2x4=0,  2x1+2x2+x3+x4=0}.

  1. Find a basis of U.
  2. Run the parametric-to-implicit algorithm on your basis, and check that the resulting equations have the same solution set as the given ones, by comparing row spaces.

exr-hyperplanes-and-systems-b3.title: B3: Two planes in \nR^4
exr-hyperplanes-and-systems-b3.title_html: B3: Two planes in R4
exr-hyperplanes-and-systems-b3.html:
Let U=span((1,0,0,1),(0,1,1,0)) and W=span((1,1,0,0),(0,0,1,1)) in R4.

  1. Find two equations for U and two for W.
  2. Use them to find U∩W.
  3. Find a single equation for U+W, using (U+W)0=U0∩W0.

exr-hyperplanes-and-systems-c1.title: C1: Avoiding finitely many subspaces
exr-hyperplanes-and-systems-c1.html:
Let F be an infinite field, V a vector space over F with 1≤dim⁡V=n<∞, and U1,…,Uk proper subspaces of V.

  1. Prove that for each i there is a non-zero φi∈V∗ with Ui⊆kerφi.
  2. Let (b1,…,bn) be a basis of V, and for t∈F put v(t)=b1+tb2+t2b3+⋯+tn−1bn. Show that t↦φi(v(t)) is given by a non-zero polynomial of degree at most n−1.
  3. Deduce that some vector of V lies in none of U1,…,Uk. In other words, V is not a union of finitely many proper subspaces.
  4. Show that the hypothesis that F is infinite cannot be dropped: over Fq, the space Fq2 is the union of q+1 proper subspaces.

Hint: for (c), use @lem-root-bound.

exr-hyperplanes-and-systems-c2.title: C2: The least number of equations for a system
exr-hyperplanes-and-systems-c2.title_html: C2: The least number of equations for a system
exr-hyperplanes-and-systems-c2.html:
Let A∈Mm×n(F) and b∈Fm, and suppose the solution set S of Ax=b is non-empty.

  1. Prove that if B∈Mp×n(F), c∈Fp and Bx=c has the same solution set S, then nul(B)=nul(A).
  2. Deduce that every system with solution set S has at least rankA equations, and that some system with solution set S has exactly rankA equations.
  3. Show by an example that (b) fails without the hypothesis S≠∅.

exr-linear-functionals-a1.title: A1
exr-linear-functionals-a1.html:
1. Define a linear functional on a vector space V over F, and the dual space V∗.
  2. True or false: p↦p(1)2 is a linear functional on R[x]. Justify your answer.
  3. True or false: if (v1,v2) and (v1,w2) are bases of V, then the first functionals of their dual bases are equal. Justify your answer.
  4. What is dim⁡M2×3(F)∗?
  5. State the formula that expresses φ∈V∗ in the dual basis of (v1,…,vn).
  6. Name the move you would use to prove that a vector v of a finite-dimensional space is 0 without computing v itself.

exr-linear-functionals-b1.title: B1: Finding dual bases
exr-linear-functionals-b1.html:
1. Find the dual basis of ((1,0,1),(0,1,1),(1,1,1)) in R3.
  2. Show that the dual basis of (1,x−1,(x−1)2) in R[x]≤2 is p↦p(1), p↦p′(1), p↦12p″(1). Hence write p=2+3x−x2 in this basis.

exr-linear-functionals-b2.title: B2: Which maps are functionals?
exr-linear-functionals-b2.html:
Determine which of the following are linear functionals. Justify your answer.

  1. R3→R, (x,y,z)↦2x−z.
  2. R3→R, (x,y,z)↦xy.
  3. M2(R)→R, A↦a12−3a21.
  4. R[x]→R, p↦∫01tp(t)dt.
  5. R[x]≤2→R, p↦p(0)+p′(0)+1.
  6. C2→C, (z,w)↦z+w―, where C2 is a vector space over C.

exr-linear-functionals-b3.title: B3: Coordinates of a functional
exr-linear-functionals-b3.html:
1. Let (φ1,φ2) be the dual basis of ((1,1),(1,−1)) from @exm-dual-basis-inverse-rows. Write ψ(x,y)=3x+5y as a combination of φ1 and φ2.
  2. Let (φ0,φ1,φ2) be the dual basis of (1,x,x2) from @exm-dual-basis-polynomials. Write ι(p)=∫01p(t)dt as a combination of them.

exr-linear-functionals-c1.title: C1: Functionals with the same kernel
exr-linear-functionals-c1.title_html: C1: Functionals with the same kernel
exr-linear-functionals-c1.html:
Let V be any vector space over F, and let φ,ψ∈V∗ with kerφ=kerψ. Prove that ψ=cφ for some c∈F. Is the converse true?

Hint: if φ≠0, fix u with φ(u)=1 and consider v−φ(v)u.

exr-linear-functionals-c2.title: C2: Functionals vanishing where others vanish
exr-linear-functionals-c2.title_html: C2: Functionals vanishing where others vanish
exr-linear-functionals-c2.html:
Let V be a vector space over F, and let φ1,…,φk,ψ∈V∗.

  1. Prove that if kerφ1∩⋯∩kerφk⊆kerψ, then ψ∈span(φ1,…,φk).
  2. Deduce that if V is finite-dimensional, then (φ1,…,φk) spans V∗ if and only if kerφ1∩⋯∩kerφk={0}.

Hint: for (a), consider the linear map T:V→Fk, v↦(φ1(v),…,φk(v)).

exr-linear-functionals-c3.title: C3: Evaluations as a dual basis
exr-linear-functionals-c3.title_html: C3: Evaluations as a dual basis
exr-linear-functionals-c3.html:
Let n∈N.

  1. Let x0,…,xn∈F be distinct. Prove that the evaluations (εx0,…,εxn) form a basis of F[x]≤n∗, and that they are the dual basis of some basis of F[x]≤n.
  2. Over F2 with n=2, show that the evaluations at the elements of F2 do not span F2[x]≤2∗.

Hint: for (a), use @thm-interpolation-unique to build the basis first.

exr-linear-functionals-c4.title: C4: How large is F\lbrack x\rbrack^{*}?
exr-linear-functionals-c4.title_html: C4: How large is F[x]∗?
exr-linear-functionals-c4.html:
Let FN be the space of sequences with entries in F.

  1. Prove that Φ:F[x]∗→FN, φ↦(φ(1),φ(x),φ(x2),…), is an isomorphism.
  2. Identify Φ(φk) for the coordinate functionals φk of @prp-coordinate-functionals-do-not-span, and Φ(ε1). Explain how @prp-coordinate-functionals-do-not-span matches @exm-sequence-standard-vectors.

Hint: for surjectivity, remember that a polynomial has only finitely many non-zero coefficients.

lem-subspace-cut-out-by-annihilator.title: A subspace is cut out by its annihilator
lem-subspace-cut-out-by-annihilator.title_html: A subspace is cut out by its annihilator
lem-subspace-cut-out-by-annihilator.html: Let V be a finite-dimensional vector space and U a subspace. For v∈V, v∈U⟺φ(v)=0 for every φ∈U0. If (φ1,…,φk) is a basis of U0, then U=kerφ1∩⋯∩kerφk.

prp-affine-subspace-intersection.title: Cosets as intersections of affine hyperplanes
prp-affine-subspace-intersection.title_html: Cosets as intersections of affine hyperplanes
prp-affine-subspace-intersection.html: Let U be a subspace of Fn of dimension k<n, and let p∈Fn. Let A∈M(n−k)×n(F) be as in @thm-subspace-is-solution-set (a), with rows a1T,…,an−kT. Then p+U={x∈Fn:Ax=Ap}=⋂i=1n−k{x:aiTx=aiTp}, an intersection of n−k affine hyperplanes.

prp-annihilator-subspace.title: The Annihilator Is a Subspace
prp-annihilator-subspace.html: Let V be a vector space over F, and let S⊆V. Then S0 is a subspace of V∗.

prp-coordinate-functionals-do-not-span.title: The Coordinate Functionals Do Not Span F[x]^{*}
prp-coordinate-functionals-do-not-span.title_html: The Coordinate Functionals Do Not Span F[x]∗
prp-coordinate-functionals-do-not-span.html: The functionals φk (k∈N) lie in F[x]∗ and form a linearly independent set. But they do not span F[x]∗: the evaluation ε1:p↦p(1) is not a linear combination of finitely many φk.

prp-nonzero-functional-surjective.title: A Non-Zero Functional Is Surjective
prp-nonzero-functional-surjective.html: Let V be a vector space over F, and let φ∈V∗ be non-zero. Then φ is surjective. If V is finite-dimensional, then dim⁡kerφ=dim⁡V−1.

thm-annihilator-properties.title: Properties of Annihilators
thm-annihilator-properties.html:
Let V be a vector space over F.

  1. If S⊆T⊆V, then T0⊆S0.
  2. For every subset S⊆V, S0=(spanS)0.
  3. For subspaces U,W of V, (U+W)0=U0∩W0.
  4. If V is finite-dimensional, then for subspaces U,W of V, (U∩W)0=U0+W0.

thm-dimension-annihilator.title: Dimension of the Annihilator
thm-dimension-annihilator.html: Let V be a finite-dimensional vector space over F, and let U be a subspace of V. Then dim⁡U+dim⁡U0=dim⁡V. More precisely, if (u1,…,um,vm+1,…,vn) is a basis of V extending a basis (u1,…,um) of U, with dual basis (φ1,…,φn), then (φm+1,…,φn) is a basis of U0.

thm-double-dual-isomorphism.title: The Double Dual Isomorphism
thm-double-dual-isomorphism.html: Let V be a finite-dimensional vector space over F. Then the evaluation map evV:V→V∗∗ is an isomorphism. Moreover, if B=(v1,…,vn) is a basis of V with dual basis B∗=(φ1,…,φn), then (evv1,…,evvn) is the dual basis of B∗.

thm-dual-basis.title: The Dual Basis
thm-dual-basis.html:
Let V be a finite-dimensional vector space over F, and let B=(v1,…,vn) be a basis of V.

  1. There are unique φ1,…,φn∈V∗ with φi(vj)=δij for all i,j. For every v∈V, φi(v) is the i-th entry of [v]B.
  2. The list (φ1,…,φn) is a basis of V∗.
  3. For every v∈V and every φ∈V∗, v=∑i=1nφi(v)vi,φ=∑i=1nφ(vi)φi.

thm-dual-map-properties.title: Properties of the Dual Map
thm-dual-map-properties.html:
Let U,V,W be vector spaces over F.

  1. For S,T∈L(V,W) and a,b∈F, (aS+bT)′=aS′+bT′.
  2. For T∈L(U,V) and S∈L(V,W), (ST)′=T′S′.
  3. (idV)′=idV∗.
  4. If T∈L(V,W) is invertible, then T′ is invertible and (T′)−1=(T−1)′.

thm-dual-of-quotient.title: Dual of a Quotient
thm-dual-of-quotient.html: Let V be a vector space over F, of any dimension, let U be a subspace, and let π:V→V/U be the quotient map. Then the dual map π′:(V/U)∗→V∗,π′(ψ)=ψ∘π, is injective, and its image is U0. Hence π′ is an isomorphism from (V/U)∗ onto U0, and (V/U)∗≅U0.

thm-dual-of-subspace.title: Dual of a Subspace
thm-dual-of-subspace.html: Let V be a vector space over F, of any dimension, and let U be a subspace of V. The restriction map ρ:V∗→U∗, ρ(φ)=φ|U, is linear and surjective, and kerρ=U0. Hence V∗/U0→U∗,φ+U0↦φ|U is a well-defined isomorphism, and U∗≅V∗/U0.

thm-evaluation-map-linear-injective.title: The Evaluation Map Is Linear and Injective
thm-evaluation-map-linear-injective.title_html: The Evaluation Map Is Linear and Injective
thm-evaluation-map-linear-injective.html: Let V be any vector space over F. Then the evaluation map evV:V→V∗∗ is linear and injective.

thm-evaluation-natural.title: The Evaluation Map Is Natural
thm-evaluation-natural.html: Let V and W be vector spaces over F, and let T∈L(V,W). Then T″evV=evWT. That is, T″(evv)=evTv for every v∈V. If V and W are finite-dimensional, then T″=evWTevV−1.

thm-functionals-on-fn.title: Functionals on F^n Are Row Vectors
thm-functionals-on-fn.title_html: Functionals on Fn Are Row Vectors
thm-functionals-on-fn.html: For a=(a1,…,an)∈Fn, define φa:Fn→F by φa(x):=aTx=a1x1+⋯+anxn. Then φa∈(Fn)∗. Every φ∈(Fn)∗ equals φa for exactly one a, namely a=(φ(e1),…,φ(en)). The map Fn→(Fn)∗, a↦φa, is an isomorphism.

thm-functionals-separate-points.title: Functionals Separate Vectors
thm-functionals-separate-points.html:
Let V be a finite-dimensional vector space over F.

  1. If v∈V and v≠0, then there is φ∈V∗ with φ(v)=1.
  2. If v∈V satisfies φ(v)=0 for every φ∈V∗, then v=0. It suffices that φi(v)=0 for the functionals φi of one dual basis.
  3. For u,w∈V: u=w if and only if φ(u)=φ(w) for every φ∈V∗.

thm-hyperplane-kernel-functional.title: Hyperplanes Are Kernels of Functionals
thm-hyperplane-kernel-functional.html: Let V be a vector space over F, of any dimension, and let H be a subspace of V. Then H is a hyperplane if and only if H=kerφ for some non-zero φ∈V∗.

thm-independent-functionals-surjective.title: Independent Functionals
thm-independent-functionals-surjective.html:
Let V be a vector space over F, of any dimension, and let φ1,…,φk∈V∗. The following are equivalent:

  1. (φ1,…,φk) is linearly independent in V∗;
  2. Φ:V→Fk is surjective;
  3. kerφ1∩⋯∩kerφk has codimension exactly k.

thm-kernel-image-dual-map.title: Kernel and Image of the Dual Map
thm-kernel-image-dual-map.title_html: Kernel and Image of the Dual Map
thm-kernel-image-dual-map.html:
Let V and W be vector spaces over F, and let T∈L(V,W).

  1. kerT′=(imT)0.
  2. If V and W are finite-dimensional, then imT′=(kerT)0.

thm-matrix-of-dual-map.title: The Matrix of the Dual Map Is the Transpose
thm-matrix-of-dual-map.title_html: The Matrix of the Dual Map Is the Transpose
thm-matrix-of-dual-map.html: Let V and W be finite-dimensional vector spaces over F, with ordered bases B of V and C of W, and let B∗ and C∗ be their dual bases. For every T∈L(V,W), [T′]C∗B∗=([T]BC)T.

thm-parametric-to-implicit.title: Correctness of the Conversion
thm-parametric-to-implicit.html: Let v1,…,vp∈Fn, U=span(v1,…,vp), and let M and A be as in the algorithm. Then nul(A)=U, and A has exactly d=n−dim⁡U rows, which are linearly independent.

thm-row-space-annihilates-null-space.title: The Row Space Is the Annihilator of the Null Space
thm-row-space-annihilates-null-space.title_html: The Row Space Is the Annihilator of the Null Space
thm-row-space-annihilates-null-space.html: Let A∈Mm×n(F). Identifying a row vector aT∈M1×n(F) with the functional φa∈(Fn)∗, {φa:aT∈row(A)}=nul(A)0. Consequently dim⁡row(A)+dim⁡nul(A)=n.

thm-subspace-is-solution-set.title: Every Subspace Is a Solution Set
thm-subspace-is-solution-set.title_html: Every Subspace Is a Solution Set
thm-subspace-is-solution-set.html:
Let U be a subspace of Fn with dim⁡U=k.

  1. There is a matrix A∈M(n−k)×n(F) with U=nul(A). One may take as rows of A the vectors a1T,…,an−kT for any ai∈Fn such that (φa1,…,φan−k) is a basis of U0.
  2. If B∈Mm×n(F) and nul(B)=U, then m≥n−k.

So U is the solution set of a homogeneous system of exactly n−k=codimU equations, and of no system with fewer. (When k=n, that is U=Fn, this is the empty system, with no equations.)
